title: Systems in the Human Body
summary: The structure and functions of the digestive, respiratory, circulatory, excretory and nervous systems, and how they work together.

notes.text: The human body has several **organ systems**. Each has its own job, but they depend on each other. For example, the digestive system supplies glucose and the respiratory system supplies oxygen; the circulatory system carries both to every cell for respiration.

Digestion breaks large food molecules into small, soluble molecules that can be absorbed into the blood. **Mechanical digestion** is the physical breaking up of food (chewing, churning); **chemical digestion** uses **enzymes**.

rows: Teeth chew food; saliva contains an enzyme that starts digesting starch
Muscular tube that moves food to the stomach by peristalsis (waves of muscle contraction)
Churns food; acid kills germs; enzymes start digesting protein
Makes bile, which breaks fats into small droplets
Completes digestion; villi absorb nutrients into the blood

notes.text: Air enters through the **nose** (where it is warmed, moistened and filtered), passes down the **trachea** (windpipe), into two **bronchi**, then smaller **bronchioles**, and finally reaches millions of tiny air sacs called **alveoli**. In the alveoli, **gaseous exchange** takes place: oxygen diffuses into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out.

Increases, so air is pushed out

notes.text: The **heart** pumps **blood** through **blood vessels** to every part of the body. Humans have a **double circulation**: the right side of the heart pumps blood to the lungs to collect oxygen, and the left side pumps oxygen-rich blood to the rest of the body.

rows: Thick, muscular, elastic walls; high pressure
Thinner walls; valves stop backflow; low pressure
Between arteries and veins, through tissues
Walls one cell thick, so substances can diffuse in and out

items: **Plasma** is the liquid part; it carries dissolved food, carbon dioxide, hormones and waste.

notes.text: **Excretion** is the removal of waste made by the body's cells. The **kidneys** filter urea and excess water from the blood to make urine; the **lungs** excrete carbon dioxide; the **skin** removes some water and salts in sweat.

The **nervous system** (brain, spinal cord and nerves) receives information from the sense organs and coordinates responses. A **reflex action**, such as pulling your hand away from a hot stove, is fast and automatic because the message goes through the spinal cord without waiting for the brain.

notes.label: Common mistake
notes.text: Excretion (removing waste made by cells, such as urea and CO₂) is not the same as egestion (removing undigested food as faeces).
